chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by polemical address, moral examples, and Christianized/judgment language (strong application drift in the second half). The only clear recoverable substrate fragment is the bare cosmological axiom of the Two Essences (Light/Darkness) embedded in a hagiographic-looking frame sentence.

paragraphs.core_text: the] two essences that are present at the beginning [ ... ] the Light and the Darkness, that which is good and that which is evi[], life and] death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame wrapper describing a visionary scene and speech-introduction ("Once again, when our father looked... [He] says...") as later hagiographic/compilational framing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The extracted clause is a compact, impersonal cosmological axiom (Two Essences at the beginning) characteristic of the dualist substrate; the surrounding visionary-narrative and speech-introduction is frame material.
Second-person address and argumentative setup against monotheists ("you... among you... they say") anchors the discourse in a contemporary dispute rather than cosmos→cosmos exposition.

Catalog of social/moral evils (lying, slander, adultery, theft, idol-worship, Mammon, etc.) functions as polemical illustration in the editor’s present world, not as a systematic cosmological mapping.
Direct exhortation/imperatives and threat logic ("why do you annul... do them!... woes") is application-voice ethical polemic, not substrate cosmology.

Argumentation is tied to Christianized authority language ("beloved son", "apostles") and a tree/fruit proof-text trajectory; this enters the Kephalaia through Mani’s/Manichaean Christian synthesis rather than the older impersonal teaching layer.

Explicitly Christian Trinitarian-style phrasing ("beloved son... holy spirit") and the five-trees/fruit saying marks a New-Testament-shaped proof-text layer (even if paraphrased rather than introduced by a formal citation formula).
Eschatological condemnation scene with "beloved son", "holy spirit", "last day", "advent" is Christian overlay in exhortation mode.

Continues judgment/exhortation ("I have recounted to you... Judge of truth") in application voice; framed as impending adjudication rather than cosmological mechanism, consistent with late overlay/paraenesis.
